title: [CPU] Fix wrongly causal-masked bidirectional attention
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

On the Intel AMX CPU attention backend, `extend_attention_cpu` always masked the extend stage of attention as causal. This is correct for decoder-style self-attention, but wrong for bidirectional, encoder-only self-attention (e.g. BERT-family rerankers/embedders like bge-reranker). On this backend such models silently got causally-masked attention scores, producing incorrect outputs.

When running `BAAI/bge-reranker-base` on CPU:
For the below request:
```
{
  "model": "BAAI/bge-reranker-base",
  "query": "what is panda?",
  "documents": [
    "hi",
    "The giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca), sometimes called a panda bear or simply panda, is a bear species endemic to China."
  ],
  "return_documents": true
}
```
Before this fix:
`"hi"` and  `"The giant panda ..."` both get the same score: 2.611328125, which is not reasonble.

After this fix:
Scores diverge correctly, matching what a real cross-encoder should produce:
`"The giant panda ..."`: score is 6.1875
`"hi"`: score is -8.15625

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
- `python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/cpu/extend.cpp`: add an `is_causal` parameter (default `true`) to `extend_attention_cpu`. The stage-2 loop now iterates over the full extend range and only applies the causal mask when `is_causal` is set, instead of unconditionally limiting keys to `[0, m + BLOCK_M)` and masking `n + n_size - 1 > m`.

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/intel_amx_backend.py`: compute `is_causal = not (layer.is_cross_attention or layer.attn_type == AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY)` and pass it into `extend_attention_fwd`, mirroring the existing pattern in `triton_backend.py`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/ee1f2e8dfdbb264727134aeac4b8dec155ec6efe/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/triton_backend.py#L1360-L1368.
